# Introduction

As documented [here](https://communities.sas.com/t5/SASware-Ballot-Ideas/Confidence-limits-using-the-Miettinen-Nurminen-stratified-method/idi-p/829317), there is a requirement to use methods other than the simple Approximate Normal (Wald) method, for confidence intervals (CIs) for comparing proportions from stratified datasets. In certain cases, for example, when you have a baseline imbalance of stratification factors, or when the treatment allocation scheme was stratified, it is important to control for the stratification factors. Stratified analysis may also be employed when combining the results of two pivotal trials for an Integrated Summary of Efficacy (although the validity of such a meta-analysis using only two studies may be questionable).

The stratified Miettinen-Nurminen 1985 asymptotic score method is of particular interest because it is often recommended and used by regulatory authorities for clinical trial submissions. It is particularly relevant for non-inferiority trials, where the confidence limits correspond to hypothesis tests with the variance estimated under the (non-zero) null hypothesis. A modification of the stratified score approach is provided by the Skewness-Corrected Asymptotic Score (SCAS) method, for potential improvement in type 1 error rates achieved by such one-sided tests, especially for ratio contrasts or designs with uneven treatment allocation.

Note that there are variations of the Miettinen-Nurminen method, depending on the weights used: the original version as published in the Miettinen-Nurminen 1985 paper uses an iterative weighting scheme. An alternative simpler version using Mantel-Haenszel weighting is often employed instead for RD, having been found to produce similar results in a 2008 ASA paper[@lu2008].

\[(Check & add citation - Tang2020?) - Use of either of these weighting schemes for RD and RR has been shown to be consistent with the efficient score and the CMH test for association. For the same consistency in analysis of stratified OR, it is necessary to use INV weights instead of MH.\]

Alternative methods for a stratified CI include the Approximate Normal (Mantel-Haenszel with Sato variance estimate), Summary Score, Stratified Newcome, and Klingenberg methods.

# Packages

There are four identified packages on CRAN with functions that can produce a stratified MN CI in R.

- [{ratesci}](https://cran.r-project.org/package=ratesci) - `scoreci(..., stratified = TRUE)` for stratified RD, RR and OR, with either MN, MH or IVS weighting. Includes optional skewness correction via the `skew = TRUE` argument.
- [{cicalc}](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/cicalc/index.html) - `ci_prop_diff_mn_strata()` for stratified RD only, MH weighting, also with option for Summary Score method, and additional functions `ci_prop_diff_mh_strata()` and `ci_rel_risk_cmh_strata()` for the Mantel-Haenszel methods for RD and RR.
- [{sasLM}](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/cicalc/index.html) - `RDmn(), RRmn() and ORmn()` for all stratified contrasts, MN weighting. \[`RDinv(), RRinv() and ORcmh()` ...\]
- [{metalite.ae}](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/cicalc/index.html) - `rate_compare()` for stratified RD only, MH weighting applied with the `weight = "cmh"` argument.

There is also publicly-available code associated with a 2014 paper by Klingenberg at <https://sites.williams.edu/bklingen/files/2013/06/stratMHRD.r>, including the `strat.MHRD.MN` function which gives the MN CI for RD using either MN or MH weights.

The table below indicates which methods can be produced using each package, for stratified RD and RR:

| Method | Weights | ratesci | cicalc | sasLM | Klingenberg | metalite.ae |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|----------|------------|-----------|
| **MN** | MN | RD,RR | \- | RD,RR | RD# | \- |
|  | MH | RD,RR | RD | \- | RD | RD |
|  | Others\* | RD,RR |  | RD,RR | RD | \- |
| **SCAS** | All | RD,RR | \- | \- | \- | \- |
| **Mantel-Haenszel / Sato** | MH | \- | RD,RR | \- | RD | \- |
| **Summary Score** | IV (pseudo variance) | \- | RD | \- | \- | \- |
| **Stratified Newcombe** | MH, \[Wilson?\] | \- | RD | \- | \- | \- |
| **Klingenberg** | MH | \- | \- | \- | RD | \- |

: \*e.g. Crude inverse variance, sample size, equal, or user-defined custom weights\
#Klingenberg's implementation of MN weights does not recalculate the weights at each iteration

\[For stratified odds ratio, the MH weighting is not consistent with the efficient score. Here, it is recommended to use either MN weights, or weights based on the inverse variance derived from the constrained MLEs of p1 and p2 for each selected value of delta - this option is implemented in `ratesci::scoreci(..., weighting = "INV")`. Some packages (such as `sasLM::ORinv`) instead use the inverse variance derived from the crude stratum point estimates of p1 and p2, leading to discrepancies in results. Furthermore, `sasLM::ORmn()` claims to apply MN weights, but the output does not match with `ratesci::scoreci(..., weighting = "MN")`. Errors in the `sasLM` source code were noted in [@laud2025] - the package maintainers have addressed the issues raised for `RDmn()` and `RRmn()`, but inconsistencies remain for `ORmn()`.\]

This page is a placeholder whilst further content is being developed. Running code as shown below was found to give the same results in the examples tested.

## {ratesci}

```         
NOTE that: skew = FALSE option, indicates no skewness correction which gives us the stratified Miettinen-Nurminen method. 

NOTE: The data contain aggregated counts with 1 row per stratum of results.
Eg.
strata  x1  n1  x2  n2
grp1    5   10  3   12
grp2    1   3   7   15
etc.



ratesci_out <- scoreci(
    x1 = strat_counts$x1,  #n events in trt 1 (Active)
    n1 = strat_counts$n1,  #n subjects in trt 1 (Active)
    x2 = strat_counts$x2,  #n events in trt 2 (comparator/placebo)
    n2 = strat_counts$n2,  #n subjects in trt2 (comparator/placebo)
    distrib = "bin",  #binomial distribution
    contrast = "RD",  #risk difference
    level = 0.95, # 95% ci
    skew = FALSE, # disable skewness to get MN method
    stratified = TRUE, #combine strata
    weighting = "MH", #MH method as reccomended by MN method
  )
```

## {cicalc}

```         
NOTE: set resp as: 1 = responder (event of interest), 0 = non-responders
      set trt as: 0= Numerator Active, 1= Denominator Comparator/Placebo
      set strat as: 
NOTE: The data are not aggregated, there is 1 row per subject identifying their trt, resp and strat categorization
Eg.
subj  strat   resp  trt
1     grp1    1     1
2     grp1    0     0
3     grp1    1     0
etc

NOTE: The following implements stratified mittinen nurminen
cicalc_out <- ci_prop_diff_mn_strata(
  x = resp, 
  by = trt, 
  strata = strat, 
  data = dataqc2
  )
  
  
NOTE: Other options are available - see package for more detail:
ci_prop_diff_mn_strata(
  x,
  by,
  strata,
  method = c("score", "summary score"),
  conf.level = 0.95,
  delta = NULL,
  data = NULL
)
```
